title: Sangam Literature

cards.b: Sangam literature is the main source for the first centuries CE in the Tamil south. Prelims asks about the three sangams, anthologies, epics and kings. It also appears in questions on classical languages.

Tradition speaks of three Sangams at Madurai: First (lost), Second at Kapatapuram, Third at Madurai (Pandya patronage). Only the Third survives. Dates: c. 300 BCE to 300 CE (various). Nakkirar, Kapilar, Paranar, Auvaiyar are poets. Tolkappiyam by Tolkappiyar, the oldest Tamil grammar.

Ettuthogai (Eight Anthologies): Narrinai, Kuruntokai, Ainkurunuru, Patirruppattu, Paripadal, Kalittokai, Akananuru, Purananuru. Pattuppattu (Ten Idylls): Tirumurugarruppadai, Porunararruppadai, Mullaippattu, Pattinappalai, Maduraikkanci, etc. Pathinenkilkanakku: 18 minor works including the Tirukkural by Thiruvalluvar.

Akam poems are about love (five tinais: kurinji hills, mullai forest, marutham plain, neithal coast, palai desert). Puram poems are about war, kings, charity and public life. The Purananuru praises kings such as Karikala and Nedunjeliyan; Pattinappalai describes Puhar.

The Five Great Epics: Silappadikaram (Ilango Adigal, story of Kovalan, Kannagi, Madhavi), Manimekalai (Sittalai Sattanar, Buddhist), Sivaka Chintamani (Tiruttakkadevar, Jain), Valayapathi, Kundalakesi. Silappadikaram and Manimekalai are the two twin epics; Kannagi worshipped as Pattini in Sri Lanka.

Three dynasties: Cholas (Uraiyur, Puhar; Karikala), Cheras (Vanji; Senguttuvan), Pandyas (Madurai; Nedunjeliyan). Trade with Rome from Muziris, Arikamedu, Puhar. Chieftains (the Velirs) and bards (panar, viralis) received gifts. Brahmins, hero stones (nadukal) and Murugan worship are documented.

Scholars disagree on dating. Kamil Zvelebil and K. A. Nilakanta Sastri accept 1st to 3rd century CE for core works. The “Sangam” as an academy is a later tradition. Tamil was given classical language status in 2004, the first language so honoured.

Tirukkural is widely used in public life; a Thiruvalluvar statue stands at Kanyakumari (133 ft). Keezhadi excavations near Madurai, Tamil Nadu, link Sangam-age urban life; the state released results of early dating to the 6th century BCE. Tamil Nadu Archaeology Department runs a site museum there.

• “Sangam literature is a mirror of society. Discuss.”
  • Prelims: author-work matches (Ilango Adigal, Thiruvalluvar); two Tamil classical dynasties; 2004.
  • Use evidence: poems, Roman gold coins, Keezhadi.
